clue.text: Disreputable press cited for contempt

indicators.note: a disreputable press is in disorder, so these words are shuffled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scandal sheet is hauled up before a court for contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disreputable' looks like a description of the press, but it is the anagram signal working on PRESS CITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing disrespect is treating someone with scorn, which is what contempt means.

clue.text: It's about time for a piece of news

indicators.note: about here means turned around and rearranged, so the next word is shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone decides the moment has come for a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is a link (it is); 'about' rearranges TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is a single report or story in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Primate replaces the ushers

indicators.note: read as re-places, the word ushers has its letters placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A monkey takes over from the theatre ushers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' is split as re-places: put the letters of USHERS in a new order. 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus is a macaque monkey, a kind of primate much used in research.

clue.text: Poet to serve as a good model?

definitions.text: to serve as a good model?

explanation.surface: A question whether a poet could be a good artist's model.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell (or her brothers Osbert and Sacheverell) was an English poet; split into two words, the name means to pose well for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell was a celebrated English writer of verse, and to sit well is to pose nicely for an artist.

clue.text: Learning Heather goes out to work for a living

indicators.note: the heather leaves, so its letters are taken out of the first word

parts.note: taken as written; the remaining letters lying together inside it is a coincidence of the deletion, not a hidden word
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A student named Heather drops out of education to get a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a girl's name but is the plant LING; its letters L, I, N, G come out of LEARNING in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain money through labour, which is working for a living.

clue.text: For wrapping or handkerchiefs-its uses are varied

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thin paper serves many purposes, from parcels to blowing noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are varied' rearranges ITS USES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue paper is used to wrap delicate goods, and paper tissues serve as disposable hankies.

clue.text: Light and delicate piano had us quite excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pianist's gentle playing thrilled the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite excited' scrambles PIANO HAD US.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaphanous fabric is so fine and sheer that light shows through it.

clue.text: It causes rough weather and loss of trade

explanation.surface: Something brings bad weather and a business downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pressure system brings storms, and an economic slump means a long fall in business activity.

clue.text: Fish spear?

explanation.surface: A fish that could be a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater predator with long jaws, and an old infantry weapon with a long shaft and pointed head.

clue.text: Shares exist in false teeth

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside another

parts.note: dentures are sets of false teeth
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A claim that stocks are lurking inside someone's false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Debentures are loan stocks issued by a company, traded like other securities.

clue.text: He wrote for various papers

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take different forms, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist contributed to several newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: SAPPER was the pen name of H. C. McNeile, author of the Bulldog Drummond thrillers; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of the British thriller writer H. C. McNeile, creator of Bulldog Drummond.

clue.text: Letter that is spelt badly

indicators.note: badly arranged letters are out of order, so these are shuffled

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A complaint that a letter contains spelling mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles IE (that is) with SPELT together.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal written message, such as those in the New Testament.

clue.text: Creatures that ruin the mar rows

indicators.note: to ruin the letters is to wreck their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pests that spoil the rows of vegetable marrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' rearranges THE MAR ROWS; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms are burrowing animals of the soil.

clue.text: One is certain to be this

definitions.text: One is certain to be this

parts.words: One is certain to be this
parts.note: read 'one' as a person who is always right: someone incapable of error is sure of being so

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is bound to be something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being incapable of error means being certain never to be wrong.

clue.text: We hear school meals should be this

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: Eton College is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A comment that school dinners ought to be finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the English boarding school; said aloud it sounds like a word for consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals are meant to be consumed, gone down the throat.

clue.text: Breaks faith and gambles about Ray

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: bets are gambles or wagers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler named Ray lets his friends down.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone is to be disloyal and break trust with them.

clue.text: Should it be made from brush wood?

definitions.text: Should it be made from brush wood?

parts.words: Should it be made from brush wood?
parts.note: brushwood is twigs and small branches, the traditional material for a garden broom

explanation.surface: A question whether something should be made of twigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom of twigs tied to a handle, made from brushwood.

clue.text: The ways of country folk

parts.note: 'ways' suggests habits but means roads: the narrow roads that country people travel

explanation.surface: A remark on the customs of rural people.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow rural roads, bordered by hedges, are the routes country people use.

clue.text: Craft lacking a prow?

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so the word loses its front letter

explanation.surface: A boat without a pointed front.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a flat floating platform is a craft with no prow, and the word loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple flat vessel of logs or planks has no shaped bow.

clue.text: One gentile about to become a Hindu ascetic

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for gentile is written backwards

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A non-Jew turns to Hindu asceticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu holy man who practises meditation and self-denial.

clue.text: Singer gets an awkward note right

indicators.note: an awkward note is one twisted out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist finally hits a tricky note correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges NOTE; 'gets an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A male voice above baritone, or the man who sings in it.

clue.text: Growing form of elation

indicators.note: a form of a word is a version of it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Elation keeps taking new shapes as it grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ELATION. 'Growing' is the definition read as a noun phrase: something that grows, as in an ingrowing one.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plate on each foot digit grows constantly and must be trimmed.

clue.text: Still in a terrible fluster

indicators.note: a terrible state is a mess, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone remains motionless while in a dreadful panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges FLUSTER; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means calm and quiet, untroubled.

clue.text: Can holy orders be so calm and peaceful?

indicators.note: to order letters is to put them in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Can holy orders be so calm and peaceful?
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' looks like the religious life but rearranges CAN HOLY; 'be so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are a time of tranquillity, named after a bird said to calm the sea.

clue.text: Chinatown seems in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are jumbled, so these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Chinese quarter seems to be in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinatown' is read as china town: the German town that gives its name to fine porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Saxon town whose factory has made Europe's best-known porcelain since 1710.

clue.text: Having the flavour of the seasons

definitions.text: Having the flavour of the seasons

parts.words: Having the flavour of the seasons
parts.note: 'seasons' looks like times of year but means seasonings such as pepper and nutmeg

explanation.surface: Something tastes of the times of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been seasoned with aromatic flavourings like cinnamon or cloves.

clue.text: Dress put on about spring

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for put on goes round the others

parts.note: clothes put on are on
a rig is a set of clothes, an outfit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dresses for the start of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan ran 'Dress' and 'I' together. 'about' wraps the word for put on round the outfit word and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a source, the place where something begins.

clue.text: Point-to point training establishment

parts.note: E is east, one of the compass points
N is north, another compass point

explanation.surface: A racing venue for point-to-point horse races.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase; here read it as compass point E, then TO, then compass point N. Eton is the English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a school, a place where boys are educated.

clue.text: Mere colour

explanation.surface: A pool that is also a hue.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a pond or small body of fresh water, and lake is also a crimson pigment.

clue.text: If I tail car clumsily it would appear contrived

indicators.note: something done clumsily is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Following a car awkwardly would look staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsily' rearranges IF I TAIL CAR; 'it would appear' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial means forced or not natural, which is what contrived means.

clue.text: Lose form in the heat

parts.note: 'lose form' suggests a sportsman off his game in hot weather, but means losing shape as a solid turns liquid

explanation.surface: An athlete struggles in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat turns a solid such as ice or wax into liquid, so it loses its shape.

clue.text: People may have to put up with them

definitions.text: People may have to put up with them

parts.words: People may have to put up with them
parts.note: 'put up with' suggests tolerate, but means lodge: lodgers are put up by the women who let them rooms

explanation.surface: A grumble about people one must tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who let rooms in their homes to paying lodgers provide them with a place to stay.
